# Receiver-generated schema-4 saved summaries

These fixtures pair retained schema-4 reports with the summary the receiver
actually derives from them. They are not hand-written evidence. The summary
bytes are byte-identical to the committed receiver outputs under
`crates/s14-receiver/tests/fixtures/s14-saved-summary-v1/`; the report bytes are
the receiver's retained source fixtures.

Generator used by the receiver worker:

```sh
cargo run --offline --locked -p htp-s14-receiver --example saved_summary -j1 -- <source_path>
```

## Provenance

- Published HTP foundation: PR84 head
  `4561cfd` ("Publish reviewed schema-4 receiver foundation with admission
  closed"), branch `wave1/s14-receiver-foundation`. The receiver-only source
  was first reviewed at pin `2b33f89791bc3269334b4992161f986976f8f2b4`.
- Committed example set:
  `crates/s14-receiver/tests/fixtures/s14-saved-summary-v1/` (7 summaries plus
  `manifest.json` with source/summary byte and SHA-256 pins).
- `report-complete-verified.json` and `report-partial-mixed.json` are the
  producer fixtures vendored byte-identically by the receiver from producer
  `d2a925723dcb4b03dd2063483ab9462bdf0af3a9`.
- `report-partial-omitted.json` is the receiver's retained
  `v4-candidate-mixed-omitted.json`.
- `report-violation.json` is the retained `v4-candidate-intent.json`. Its
  summary is generated by the same pinned receiver but is **not** one of the
  seven committed example summaries; it is included only because none of the
  committed examples reports a policy violation. Relay this divergence to the
  receiver owner.

## Pinned summary text digests

| Summary file | Canonical SHA-256 | Bytes |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `summary-complete-verified.json` | `284b0faac82212ed6283faf51c839a8d5e25b71fd581cd278b319458e2eb5b4d` | 7867 |
| `summary-partial-mixed.json` | `572efbada7fec9f67920ea2a4def1bfec61c51d7c35f95724415af6d393fbc9c` | 7790 |
| `summary-partial-omitted.json` | `167150c3a2b95b3608a0a2361db8ca24874a10e6d2b74df37537fcff66390895` | 7637 |
| `summary-violation.json` (extra, not in the committed set) | `9afe3ff3d307dbb193050269b595ffbe2ac5e7e37e35ab3caf62c59e76c0b4c1` | 7710 |

The digest is computed over the exact retained summary text bytes, not over
`JSON.stringify(parsedSummary)`. A parsed summary object is not receiver
canonical: PostgreSQL JSONB and ordinary object handling reorder keys, so the
serialization can differ from the receiver text even when the semantic content
is identical. The detail must carry the retained text separately from the
parsed object. See the native e2e pair below.

## Native e2e pair (JSONB-reordered parsed object)

`summary-native-e2e.json` and `report-native-e2e.json` are the genuine paired
artifacts from the local S14 receipt e2e fixture (`scripts/s14-receipt-e2e/`),
copied byte-for-byte:

| Artifact | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `summary-native-e2e.json` | 7711 | `f55ee1b3390b05a33e2001dd7b3f5891e099698d331942b9e56bf0e68c9c5b27` |
| `report-native-e2e.json` | 45958 | `2c59c8eff03997d98f7ad1c49d513a030faf6bd37fa3edbee52e76d8606e25a1` |

`summary-native-e2e.jsonb.json` is that same summary after a normal PostgreSQL
JSONB round trip (`...::jsonb::text`). It is 8257 bytes and its serialization
differs from the receiver text. The browser check serves the JSONB-reordered
object as the parsed `summary` and the raw text as `summary_text`, then asserts
the download is the raw text. The absent-text and digest-mismatch runs use the
same pair so they cannot pass by accidental round-tripping.

## Retained source binding

`source_sha256` (`sha256:<lowercase-hex>`) and `source_bytes` bind a summary to
the exact retained report bytes. They are returned beside the summary and are
**not** part of the emitted summary wire object, so the summary-v5 fixture bytes
are unchanged. The summary hash proves only the summary; compare the raw report
by its own stored digest and size. The retained summary text is returned as
`summary_text`; its digest and length are `summary_sha256` and `summary_bytes`.

| Report file | SHA-256 | Bytes |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `report-complete-verified.json` | `2443936d93da699595bdb135995e3d1d1503b96d973f5be4f3b82d9f243f4342` | 26567 |
| `report-partial-mixed.json` | `e95085661f1cbddc165e3acf47fb05a69e47bbe6c4be4dbffe480b385f15902e` | 26829 |
| `report-partial-omitted.json` | `9cd361d79c93e40ddb57b0043c201fea0090836c500dd726849d055ec6b5efe9` | 425640 |
| `report-violation.json` | `530c1c822d56ad151a8d9c17bc39b6c9a8c5ad6d103699af01917319e8e54139` | 44834 |

## What each example establishes

- `summary-complete-verified.json`: the audit aggregate is `complete_verified`
  with 82 rules verified clean and six rules with findings. The severity map
  omits `critical` because none occurred.
- `summary-partial-mixed.json`: crawl coverage is complete but evaluation
  coverage is partial, so 25 rules stay `unknown_partial`. Absence of a finding
  on those rules is not a pass.
- `summary-partial-omitted.json`: the audit is `unknown_partial`, 244 records
  and 156 observations were omitted, and the retained unknowns remain visible.
- `summary-violation.json`: the receiver reports two policy violations and two
  triggered advisories while the audit stays `unknown_partial`.

A `complete_verified` audit does not imply every rule is complete; a
`complete_verified` rule does not imply the report is globally clean.
